analysis:
Documentation-only change in docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The head side adds lines 743-747 and 751-769, which document `darkbloom update --rollback`/`--yes`. The documented behavior: it restores the retained predecessor and quarantines the installed release. It contacts no coordinator. It drains, then swaps through the watchdog's journaled rollback under the update lease. It refuses cluster pairs, foreground providers, a held lease, a missing or identical release, a mismatched app, and a kept release that fails its hash or signature check (RollbackRefusal).

Relevant threats are T-043 and T-013. T-043 says rollback authority sits in the same replaceable binary. A rollback driven by the operator is within ADV-001's existing capability, since the operator already controls the binary. The documented hash and signature check on the retained release preserves artifact integrity. Serving authorization remains governed by coordinator-side qualification (T-054, A-017), and nothing in the doc claims that rollback grants trust.

The other changed head lines (1852, 1859-1860) fall outside the supplied units, so I could not review them. Units 10 and 11 otherwise contain unchanged surrounding docs: logout, sandbox (TB-013/T-061) and addon (TB-012).

No security regression is evident from the docs themselves.

Open questions for integration:
- Whether UpdateRollback.swift and SelfUpdater+Rollback.swift actually verify the predecessor signature and hash before the swap.
- Whether they hold the update lease across the drain and swap.
- Whether the coordinator still rejects revoked or unqualified predecessor builds. A downgrade to an older, vulnerable but still-qualified build is a policy question for the platform's qualification revocation (T-054).

The threat model may warrant noting operator-initiated rollback under T-043. The implementation source was not supplied.
